s: out of touch, divorced from reality, rarefied (ignorant of the concerns of the average person, typically due to privilege and/or arrogance)
Jeder französische Staatspräsident ist abgehoben. Das ist die Institution selbst, die Präsidentschaft, das verlangt die Wählerschaft: Frankreich will einen abgehobenen Präsidenten.
Every French president is divorced from the reality of everyday life. That's the institution, the presidency, that's what the voters want: France wants a president who is divorced from reality.
to come off, to come loose, to wear off
to leave (esp. an educational institution; not necessarily by graduating)
Ich muss von der Schule abgehen.
I have to leave the school.
Das Stück ist zu Ende, die Darsteller gehen von der Bühne ab.
The play is over, the performers exit the stage.
Was geht denn zwischen euch beiden ab?
What's going on between you two?
Hier geht es ganz schön ab!
There's a lot going on here!
to rise in excitement, momentum, arousal etc. (not necessarily clearly distinguishable from the sense of mere happening)
Es geht heute richtig ab an der Börse.
The stock markets are bear bullish today.
to go wild, to pop off, to let loose (of a person; typically describing celebration or partying)
Der Kanzler ist voll abgegangen, und die Jungs auch.
The chancellor really let loose, and the lads did as well.
to be missing, to lack, to be absent
to make a control walk on or otherwise literally or figuratively pass by step by step
Ich bin noch mal das Auto abgegangen, um zu schauen, ob es ganz sauber ist.
I walked around the car to assure myself of its being completely clean.
abgehen.et: From Middle High German abegān, from Old High German abagān. Equivalent to ab- + gehen.
